459: 
460:     nb_valid_samples = be.shape(dataset)[0]
461:     replace = nb_valid_samples < n_samples
462:     sample_indices = random_state.choice(
463:         nb_valid_samples,
464:         size=n_samples,
465:         replace=replace
466:     )
467:     dists = be.pdist(
468:         dataset[sample_indices],
469:         metric="euclidean",
470:     )
471:     return be.median(dists) * be.sqrt(sz)
472: 
473: 
474: def gamma_soft_dtw(dataset, n_samples=100, random_state=None, be=None):
475:     r"""Compute gamma value to be used for GAK/Soft-DTW.
476: 
477:     This method was originally presented in [1]_.
478: 
479:     Parameters
480:     ----------
481:     dataset : array-like, shape=(n_ts, sz, d) or (n_ts, sz1) or (sz,)
482:         A dataset of time series.
483:         If shape is (n_ts, sz), the dataset is composed of univariate time series.
484:         If shape is (sz,), the dataset is composed of a unique univariate time series.
485:     n_samples : int (default: 100)
486:         Number of samples on which median distance should be estimated.
487:     random_state : integer or numpy.RandomState or None (default: None)
488:         The generator used to draw the samples. If an integer is given, it
489:         fixes the seed. Defaults to the global numpy random number generator.
490:     be : Backend object or string or None
491:         Backend. If `be` is an instance of the class `NumPyBackend` or the string `"numpy"`,
492:         the NumPy backend is used.
493:         If `be` is an instance of the class `PyTorchBackend` or the string `"pytorch"`,
494:         the PyTorch backend is used.
495:         If `be` is `None`, the backend is determined by the input arrays.
496:         See our :ref:`dedicated user-guide page <backend>` for more information.
497: 
498:     Returns
499:     -------
500:     float
501:         Suggested :math:`\gamma` parameter for the Soft-DTW.
502: 
503:     Examples
504:     --------
505:     >>> dataset = [[1, 2, 2, 3], [1., 2., 3., 4.]]
506:     >>> float(gamma_soft_dtw(dataset=dataset,
507:     ...                      n_samples=200,
508:     ...                      random_state=0))  # doctest: +ELLIPSIS
509:     8.0...
510: 
511:     See Also
512:     --------
513:     sigma_gak : Compute sigma parameter for Global Alignment kernel
514: 
515:     References
516:     ----------
517:     .. [1] M. Cuturi, "Fast global alignment kernels,"
518:        ICML 2011.
519:     """
520:     be = instantiate_backend(be, dataset)
521:     return (
522:         2.0
523:         * sigma_gak(
524:             dataset=dataset, n_samples=n_samples, random_state=random_state, be=be
525:         )
526:         ** 2
527:     )
528: 
529: 
530: def soft_dtw(ts1, ts2, gamma=1.0, be=None, compute_with_backend=False):
531:     r"""Compute Soft-DTW metric between two time series.
532: 
533:     Soft-DTW was originally presented in [1]_ and is
534:     discussed in more details in our
535:     :ref:`user-guide page on DTW and its variants<dtw>`.
536: 
537:     Soft-DTW is computed as:
538: 
539:     .. math::
540: 
541:         \text{soft-DTW}_{\gamma}(X, Y) =
542:             \min_{\pi}{}^\gamma \sum_{(i, j) \in \pi} \|X_i, Y_j\|^2
543: 
544:     where :math:`\min^\gamma` is the soft-min operator of parameter
545:     :math:`\gamma`.
546: 
547:     In the limit case :math:`\gamma = 0`, :math:`\min^\gamma` reduces to a
548:     hard-min operator and soft-DTW is defined as the square of the DTW
549:     similarity measure.
550: 
551:     Parameters
552:     ----------
553:     ts1 : array-like, shape=(sz1, d) or (sz1,)
554:         A time series.
555:         If shape is (sz1,), the time series is assumed to be univariate.
556:     ts2 : array-like, shape=(sz2, d) or (sz2,)
557:         Another time series.
558:         If shape is (sz2,), the time series is assumed to be univariate.
559:     gamma : float (default 1.)
560:         Gamma parameter for Soft-DTW.
561:     be : Backend object or string or None
562:         Backend. If `be` is an instance of the class `NumPyBackend` or the string `"numpy"`,
563:         the NumPy backend is used.
564:         If `be` is an instance of the class `PyTorchBackend` or the string `"pytorch"`,
565:         the PyTorch backend is used.
566:         If `be` is `None`, the backend is determined by the input arrays.
567:         See our :ref:`dedicated user-guide page <backend>` for more information.
568:     compute_with_backend : bool, default=False
569:         This parameter has no influence when the NumPy backend is used.
570:         When a backend different from NumPy is used (cf parameter `be`):
571:         If `True`, the computation is done with the corresponding backend.
572:         If `False`, a conversion to the NumPy backend can be used to accelerate the computation.
573: 
574:     Returns
575:     -------
576:     float
577:         Similarity
578: 
579:     Examples
580:     --------
581:     >>> float(soft_dtw([1, 2, 2, 3],
582:     ...                [1., 2., 3., 4.],
583:     ...                gamma=1.))  # doctest: +NORMALIZE_WHITESPACE +ELLIPSIS
584:     -0.89...
585:     >>> float(soft_dtw([1, 2, 3, 3],
586:     ...                [1., 2., 2.1, 3.2],
587:     ...                 gamma=0.01))  # doctest: +NORMALIZE_WHITESPACE +ELLIPSIS
588:     0.089...
589: 
590:     The PyTorch backend can be used to compute gradients:
591: 
592:     >>> import torch
593:     >>> ts1 = torch.tensor([[1.0], [2.0], [3.0]], requires_grad=True)
594:     >>> ts2 = torch.tensor([[3.0], [4.0], [-3.0]])
595:     >>> sim = soft_dtw(ts1, ts2, gamma=1.0, be="pytorch", compute_with_backend=True)
596:     >>> print(sim)
597:     tensor(41.1876, dtype=torch.float64, grad_fn=<SelectBackward0>)
598:     >>> sim.backward()
599:     >>> print(ts1.grad)
600:     tensor([[-4.0001],
601:             [-2.2852],
602:             [10.1643]])
603: 
604:     >>> ts1_2d = torch.tensor([[1.0, 1.0], [2.0, 2.0], [3.0, 3.0]], requires_grad=True)
605:     >>> ts2_2d = torch.tensor([[3.0, 3.0], [4.0, 4.0], [-3.0, -3.0]])
606:     >>> sim = soft_dtw(ts1_2d, ts2_2d, gamma=1.0, be="pytorch", compute_with_backend=True)
607:     >>> print(sim)
608:     tensor(83.2951, dtype=torch.float64, grad_fn=<SelectBackward0>)
609:     >>> sim.backward()
610:     >>> print(ts1_2d.grad)
611:     tensor([[-4.0000, -4.0000],
612:             [-2.0261, -2.0261],
613:             [10.0206, 10.0206]])
614:
